senses.meaningEn: to receive, obtain, or buy something

examples.en: Did you get my text message last night?
I need to get some milk on the way home.
examples.ko: 집에 가는 길에 우유 좀 사야 해.

senses.meaningEn: to arrive at a place

examples.en: What time do we get to the airport?
Call me when you get home, okay?

senses.note: get to + 장소. 단, get home / get there 는 to 없이 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to become or change to a certain state

examples.en: It gets cold here at night.
Don't get angry, I was just joking.

senses.note: get + 형용사: get tired, get hungry, get better. become 보다 훨씬 구어적.

senses.meaningEn: to understand something

examples.en: Sorry, I don't get it. Can you explain again?
examples.ko: 미안, 이해가 안 돼. 다시 설명해 줄래?

examples.en: Oh, now I get what you mean.

senses.meaningEn: to carry or move something or someone to another place

examples.en: Don't forget to take your umbrella today.
I'll take the kids to school this morning.
examples.ko: 오늘 아침은 내가 애들 학교에 데려다줄게.

senses.note: take 는 '여기서 저기로' 가져가다, bring 은 '이쪽으로' 가져오다.

senses.meaningEn: to travel using a bus, train, taxi, etc.

examples.en: Let's take a taxi. It's raining.
I take the subway to work every day.

senses.note: take a bus / take the train / take a taxi. ride 보다 take 가 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: to need a certain amount of time

examples.en: It takes about ten minutes to walk there.
How long does it take by bus?

senses.note: It takes + 시간 + to 동사. '걸리다'를 spend 로 쓰지 않도록 주의.

senses.meaningEn: to swallow medicine

examples.en: Take this medicine twice a day after meals.
examples.ko: 이 약은 하루 두 번 식후에 드세요.

examples.en: Did you take your pills this morning?

senses.note: 약은 eat 이 아니라 take.

senses.meaningEn: to create or prepare something

examples.en: My mom makes the best kimchi stew.
examples.ko: 우리 엄마가 김치찌개를 제일 잘 하셔.

examples.en: Can you make me a cup of coffee?
examples.ko: 커피 한 잔 타 줄 수 있어?

senses.note: make breakfast / make dinner / make a sandwich.

senses.meaningEn: to cause someone to feel or do something

examples.en: This song always makes me happy.
examples.ko: 이 노래는 항상 나를 행복하게 해.

examples.en: Don't make me laugh, I'm trying to study!

senses.note: make + 사람 + 형용사/동사원형. make me to laugh (X).

senses.meaningEn: to earn money

examples.en: How much do you make a month?
She makes good money as a nurse.
examples.ko: 그녀는 간호사로 돈을 꽤 잘 벌어.

senses.meaningEn: to own or possess something

examples.en: I have two brothers and one sister.
examples.ko: 나는 남동생 둘에 여동생 하나 있어.

examples.en: Do you have a pen I can borrow?

senses.note: 소유의 have 는 진행형으로 쓰지 않음. I'm having a car (X).

senses.meaningEn: to eat or drink something

examples.en: What do you want to have for lunch?
I usually have coffee in the morning.

senses.note: have breakfast / have a drink. eat 보다 부드러운 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to experience or suffer from something

examples.en: I have a bad headache today.
I think I have a fever. I feel hot.
examples.ko: 열이 있는 것 같아. 몸이 뜨거워.

senses.note: have a cold / have a headache / have a problem.

senses.meaningEn: to move or travel to a place

examples.en: I go to the gym after work.
Where are you going this weekend?

senses.note: go to school / go home(to 없음) / go shopping(동명사).

senses.meaningEn: to change to a worse state

examples.en: The milk will go bad if you leave it out.
My hair is going gray already.

senses.note: go bad / go wrong / go crazy 처럼 주로 나쁜 변화에 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to happen or progress in a certain way

examples.en: How did your interview go?
Everything is going well so far.

senses.note: How's it going? 은 '잘 지내?'라는 인사.

senses.meaningEn: to move toward the speaker or a place

examples.en: Can you come here for a second?
The bus is coming. Hurry up!

senses.meaningEn: to go somewhere together with the listener

examples.en: We're going to lunch. Do you want to come?
examples.ko: 우리 점심 먹으러 가는데, 같이 갈래?

examples.en: Come with me, I'll show you the way.

senses.note: 듣는 사람 쪽으로 가는 건 go 가 아니라 come. I'm coming! = 지금 가요!

senses.meaningEn: to be available in a particular form, size, or color

examples.en: Does this shirt come in a smaller size?
examples.ko: 이 셔츠 더 작은 사이즈도 나와요?

examples.en: The phone comes in three colors.
examples.ko: 이 폰은 세 가지 색상으로 나와.

senses.note: come in + 사이즈/색상. 쇼핑할 때 매우 유용한 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to change direction

examples.en: Turn left at the next corner.
Turn around, you're going the wrong way.

senses.note: turn left / turn right / turn around. 길 안내의 기본 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to become a different color, state, or age

examples.en: The leaves turn red in October.
My son turns seven next month.
examples.ko: 우리 아들은 다음 달에 일곱 살이 돼.

senses.note: turn + 색/나이. turn thirty = 서른 살이 되다.

senses.meaningEn: the time when it is your chance to do something

examples.en: It's your turn to roll the dice.
Please wait your turn in line.

senses.note: take turns = 번갈아 하다.

senses.meaningEn: to take part in a game or sport, or to have fun

examples.en: The kids are playing in the yard.
Do you want to play soccer after school?

senses.note: play soccer / play games. 구기 종목은 play, 수영·달리기는 go swimming / go running.

senses.meaningEn: to make music with an instrument

examples.en: She plays the piano really well.
I'm learning to play the guitar.

senses.note: 악기 앞에는 the: play the piano. 운동 앞에는 the 없음: play tennis.

senses.meaningEn: to make a song or video start

examples.en: Can you play that song again?
Press here to play the video.

senses.meaningEn: a story performed by actors in a theater

examples.en: We saw a play at the theater last night.
My daughter is in the school play.

senses.meaningEn: to do a job, especially for money

examples.en: I work at a bank downtown.
She works from home on Fridays.

senses.note: work at/for + 회사, work as + 직업.

senses.meaningEn: to function correctly

examples.en: The elevator isn't working again.
Does this remote work with the TV?

senses.note: 기계가 '된다/안 된다'는 work / doesn't work. 아주 자주 쓰임.

senses.meaningEn: to have the result you want

examples.en: This medicine really works for headaches.
examples.ko: 이 약은 두통에 정말 효과가 있어.

examples.en: I tried your idea, and it worked!

senses.meaningEn: a job, or the place where you do it

examples.en: I have a lot of work to do today.
What time do you leave for work?

senses.note: work 는 셀 수 없는 명사. a work (X), many works (X). 직장 하나는 a job.

senses.meaningEn: brightness, or a lamp that produces it

examples.en: Please turn off the light when you leave.
There's not enough light to read here.

senses.note: traffic light = 신호등.

senses.meaningEn: not heavy

examples.en: This bag is really light and easy to carry.
examples.ko: 이 가방은 정말 가볍고 들고 다니기 편해.

examples.en: I only had a light lunch today.

senses.note: light meal = 가벼운 식사, light rain = 가랑비.

senses.meaningEn: pale in color

examples.en: Do you have this in light blue?
She painted the room a light green.

senses.meaningEn: correct or true

examples.en: That's the right answer. Good job!
You're right, we should leave early.

senses.meaningEn: on the side of your body that is toward the east when you face north

examples.en: The bank is on your right.
I hurt my right hand yesterday.

senses.meaningEn: exactly or immediately

examples.en: Wait here. I'll be right back.
The store is right next to the station.
examples.ko: 그 가게는 역 바로 옆에 있어.

senses.note: right now = 지금 당장, right here = 바로 여기, right away = 즉시.

senses.meaningEn: okay, acceptable, or in good health

examples.en: I'm fine, thanks. How are you?
Is seven o'clock fine with you?

senses.note: That's fine. = 괜찮아요. 말투에 따라 '됐어, 그만해'라는 뉘앙스가 될 수도 있음.

senses.meaningEn: sunny and not raining

examples.en: It's a fine day for a picnic.
The weather will be fine this weekend.

senses.meaningEn: money you must pay for breaking a rule

examples.en: I got a fine for parking here.
The fine for speeding is pretty high.

senses.note: pay a fine = 벌금을 내다.

senses.meaningEn: to have a particular meaning

examples.en: What does this word mean?
A red light means you have to stop.

senses.note: What do you mean? = 무슨 말이야? 가장 많이 쓰는 되묻기 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to be serious about what you say, or to intend something

examples.en: I mean it. You did a great job.
Sorry, I didn't mean to hurt you.

senses.note: I didn't mean to... = 일부러 그런 게 아니야. 사과할 때 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: unkind or cruel

examples.en: Don't be mean to your little brother.
That was a really mean thing to say.

senses.meaningEn: to go away from a place

examples.en: What time does the train leave?
I'm leaving the office now. See you soon.

senses.note: leave for + 목적지: leave for Busan = 부산으로 떠나다.

senses.meaningEn: to let something stay in a place, or forget to take it

examples.en: Oh no, I think I'm leaving my keys at home again.
examples.ko: 이런, 또 열쇠를 집에 두고 가는 것 같아.

examples.en: Just leave the dishes. I'll do them later.
examples.ko: 설거지는 그냥 둬. 내가 나중에 할게.

senses.note: Leave me alone. = 나 좀 내버려 둬.

senses.meaningEn: to give a message for someone who is not there

examples.en: Would you like to leave a message?
Please leave your name and number.

senses.meaningEn: to fail to catch a bus, train, or chance

examples.en: Hurry, or we'll miss the bus!
I missed the last train and took a taxi.

senses.meaningEn: to feel sad because someone or something is not with you

examples.en: I miss you so much. Come visit soon.
examples.ko: 너무 보고 싶어. 빨리 놀러 와.

examples.en: Do you miss Korean food when you travel?
examples.ko: 여행 가면 한국 음식 그립지 않아?

senses.note: '보고 싶다'를 want to see 로 직역하지 말고 miss 를 쓰면 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: to not go to a class, meeting, or event

examples.en: I missed class yesterday because I was sick.
Don't miss the meeting at three.

senses.meaningEn: a set of printed pages with a cover that you read

examples.en: I'm reading a really good book right now.
examples.ko: 지금 정말 좋은 책을 읽고 있어.

examples.en: Please open your books to page ten.

senses.meaningEn: to arrange to have a seat, room, or table at a future time

examples.en: I booked a hotel room for two nights.
Should we book a table for dinner?

senses.note: book a flight / book a table / book a room. 영국·미국 모두 흔히 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to make or become different

examples.en: Can we change the meeting to Friday?
You've changed a lot since high school.
examples.ko: 너 고등학교 때 이후로 많이 변했다.

senses.note: change one's mind = 마음을 바꾸다.

senses.meaningEn: to put on different clothes

examples.en: Give me five minutes to change.
I need to change into something warmer.

senses.note: change clothes / change into + 옷.

senses.meaningEn: to get off one bus or train and get on another

examples.en: Change trains at the next station.
Do I have to change buses to get there?

senses.note: change trains / change buses 처럼 복수형을 씀.

senses.meaningEn: coins, or the money you get back when you pay too much

examples.en: Here's your change. Have a nice day.
examples.ko: 거스름돈 여기 있습니다. 좋은 하루 보내세요.

examples.en: Do you have change for a twenty?

senses.note: Keep the change. = 잔돈은 가지세요.

senses.meaningEn: to ask for food, drink, or goods

examples.en: Are you ready to order?
I ordered a pizza online last night.

senses.note: 식당에서 종업원이 Are you ready to order? 라고 물으면 I'll have... 로 답함.

senses.meaningEn: a request for food or goods

examples.en: Can I take your order?
My order hasn't arrived yet.

senses.note: place an order = 주문하다, take an order = 주문을 받다.

senses.meaningEn: the way things are arranged one after another

examples.en: Put the words in the right order.
The names are in alphabetical order.

senses.note: out of order = 고장 난 (기계에 붙은 안내문).

senses.meaningEn: to separate into pieces, or damage something

examples.en: Be careful, don't break the glass.
These plates break very easily.

senses.meaningEn: to stop working

examples.en: My phone breaks every time I drop it.
examples.ko: 내 폰은 떨어뜨릴 때마다 고장 나.

examples.en: If you press too hard, it will break.
examples.ko: 너무 세게 누르면 고장 날 거야.

senses.note: 이미 고장 난 상태는 It's broken.

senses.meaningEn: a short rest from work or study

examples.en: Let's take a ten-minute break.
We have a lunch break at noon.

senses.note: take a break = 쉬다. coffee break, lunch break.

senses.meaningEn: to phone someone

examples.en: Call me when you get there.
I'll call you back in ten minutes.

senses.note: call back = 다시 전화하다. '전화하다'에 phone to 를 붙이지 않음.

senses.meaningEn: to say someone's name loudly, or to give a name

examples.en: Mom is calling you for dinner.
My friends call me Jay.

senses.note: What do you call this in English? = 이거 영어로 뭐라고 해?

senses.meaningEn: an act of talking to someone on the phone

examples.en: I got a call from my sister.
Sorry, I have to take this call.

senses.note: make a call = 전화를 걸다, take a call = 전화를 받다.

senses.meaningEn: to look at something to make sure it is correct or okay

examples.en: Let me check my schedule first.
Did you check the door is locked?

senses.note: check in = (호텔·공항) 체크인하다, check out = 퇴실하다.

senses.meaningEn: a bill in a restaurant

examples.en: Can we get the check, please?
I'll pay the check tonight.

senses.note: 미국식은 check, 영국식은 bill.

senses.meaningEn: having a low temperature

examples.en: It's so cold outside today.
Can I have a glass of cold water?

senses.note: '춥다'는 I'm cold, 날씨는 It's cold.

senses.meaningEn: a common illness that makes you sneeze and cough

examples.en: I think I'm catching a cold.
She has a bad cold and stayed home.

senses.note: catch a cold / have a cold. 관사 a 를 꼭 붙임.

senses.meaningEn: unfriendly and showing no emotion

examples.en: Why are you being so cold to me?
He gave me a cold look and walked away.
examples.ko: 그는 나를 차갑게 쳐다보고 가 버렸어.

senses.meaningEn: costing no money

examples.en: Kids under five get in free.
The coffee is free with breakfast.

senses.note: for free = 무료로. free of charge 도 같은 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: not busy

examples.en: Are you free this Saturday?
I'm free after six today.

senses.note: free time = 여가 시간.

senses.meaningEn: not being used by anyone

examples.en: Excuse me, is this seat free?
There's a free table by the window.

senses.meaningEn: difficult to do or understand

examples.en: The math test was really hard.
It's hard to wake up early in winter.

senses.meaningEn: firm and not easy to bend or break

examples.en: This bread is too hard to eat.
examples.ko: 이 빵은 너무 딱딱해서 못 먹겠어.

examples.en: I can't sleep on a hard bed.
examples.ko: 나는 딱딱한 침대에서는 잠을 못 자.

senses.meaningEn: with a lot of effort or force

examples.en: She works very hard every day.
It's raining really hard outside right now.
examples.ko: 지금 밖에 비가 정말 세게 와.

senses.note: hardly 는 '거의 ~않다'로 뜻이 전혀 다름. work hard (O), work hardly (X).

senses.meaningEn: friendly and caring about other people

examples.en: Thank you, that's very kind of you.
My teacher is kind to everyone.

senses.note: be kind to + 사람.

senses.meaningEn: a type or group of things

examples.en: What kind of music do you like?
They sell all kinds of cheese here.

senses.meaningEn: a little, somewhat

examples.en: I'm kind of tired today.
This soup is kind of salty.

senses.note: 구어에서 kinda 로 줄여 말함. 글에서는 피함.

senses.meaningEn: coming after all the others

examples.en: This is the last question on the test.
I was the last person to leave.

senses.meaningEn: the most recent one before now

examples.en: I saw that movie last week.
What did you do last weekend?

senses.note: last week / last night 앞에는 전치사를 쓰지 않음. in last week (X).

senses.meaningEn: to continue for a period of time

examples.en: The movie lasts about two hours.
examples.ko: 그 영화는 두 시간 정도 돼.

examples.en: How long does the battery last?

senses.meaningEn: to look at something for a period of time

examples.en: We watched a movie together last night.
I like watching soccer on TV.
examples.ko: 나는 TV로 축구 보는 걸 좋아해.

senses.note: TV·영화·경기는 watch, 그냥 눈에 들어오는 건 see, 시선을 돌리는 건 look.

senses.meaningEn: a small clock you wear on your wrist

examples.en: I got a new watch for my birthday.
My watch says it's almost three.

senses.note: 벽시계는 clock, 손목시계는 watch.

senses.meaningEn: to be careful about something

examples.en: Watch your step, the floor is wet.
Watch out! A car is coming.

senses.note: Watch out! = 조심해! Watch your head = 머리 조심.

senses.meaningEn: to move something so it is no longer closed

examples.en: Can you open the window? It's hot.
Open your mouth and say ah.

senses.meaningEn: not closed, or ready for business

examples.en: Is the bank open on Saturdays?
The store is open until ten.

senses.note: '영업 중'은 open, '닫음'은 closed(close 가 아님).

senses.meaningEn: to enjoy or find something pleasant

examples.en: I really like this song.
Do you like spicy food?

senses.note: I'd like... = ~을 원해요 (주문·요청할 때 정중한 표현).

senses.meaningEn: similar to something or someone

examples.en: She looks like her mother.
It smells like fresh bread in here.
examples.ko: 여기 갓 구운 빵 냄새가 나.

senses.note: look like / sound like / feel like + 명사.

senses.meaningEn: used to ask for a description of something

examples.en: What's the weather like today?
What's your new teacher like?

senses.note: How is...? 와 비슷하지만 성격·특징을 물을 때 더 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: pleasant to look at

examples.en: What a pretty dress you're wearing!
The flowers in the garden are so pretty.

senses.meaningEn: quite, fairly

examples.en: The test was pretty easy.
I'm pretty sure he's coming.

senses.note: pretty good = 꽤 좋다. 미국 구어에서 매우 자주 쓰임.

senses.meaningEn: to lift something from a surface

examples.en: Please pick up your toys from the floor.
He picked up the phone and said hello.
examples.ko: 그는 전화기를 들고 여보세요 라고 했어.

senses.meaningEn: to go and get someone in a car

examples.en: Can you pick me up at the station?
examples.ko: 역에서 나 좀 태워 줄 수 있어?

examples.en: I pick up my kids from school at three.

senses.note: pick + 사람 + up 순서로도 씀: pick me up. 반대는 drop off(내려 주다).

senses.meaningEn: to buy or collect something, often casually

examples.en: Could you pick up some bread on your way?
examples.ko: 오는 길에 빵 좀 사 올 수 있어?

examples.en: I need to pick up my package at the post office.

senses.meaningEn: to learn something easily without much effort

examples.en: Kids pick up new words very quickly.
examples.ko: 아이들은 새 단어를 아주 빨리 익혀.

examples.en: I picked up some Spanish while traveling.

senses.meaningEn: to try to find something

examples.en: I'm looking for my keys. Have you seen them?
Are you looking for anything special today?

senses.note: '찾고 있다'(과정)는 look for, '찾았다'(결과)는 find.

senses.meaningEn: to try to get a job or find a person for a role

examples.en: My brother is looking for a new job.
examples.ko: 내 동생은 새 일자리를 구하고 있어.

examples.en: They're looking for a part-time cook.

senses.meaningEn: to get out of bed

examples.en: What time do you usually get up?
I get up at six on weekdays.

senses.note: wake up 은 눈을 뜨는 것, get up 은 실제로 침대에서 나오는 것.

senses.meaningEn: to stand up after sitting or lying

examples.en: Everyone, please get up and stretch.
Don't get up, I'll get the door.
examples.ko: 일어나지 마, 내가 문 열어 줄게.

senses.meaningEn: to make a machine or light start working

examples.en: Can you turn on the TV?
Turn the light on, it's too dark.

senses.note: turn on the TV / turn the TV on 둘 다 가능. 대명사는 turn it on 만 가능.

senses.meaningEn: to make water or gas start flowing

examples.en: Turn on the hot water for the bath.
Don't turn on the gas yet.

senses.meaningEn: to make a machine, light, or water stop

examples.en: Turn off your phone during the movie.
examples.ko: 영화 보는 동안 폰 꺼 줘.

examples.en: Did you turn off the water in the bathroom?

senses.note: turn off 는 전원·물·가스 모두 가능. switch off 도 같은 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: to leave the road you are driving on

examples.en: Turn off at the next exit.
We turned off the highway to get gas.

senses.meaningEn: to place clothes or glasses on your body

examples.en: Put on your coat, it's cold outside.
Let me put my shoes on first.

senses.note: 입는 동작은 put on, 입고 있는 상태는 wear. I'm putting on a hat (동작) vs I'm wearing a hat (상태).

senses.meaningEn: to spread cream or makeup on your skin

examples.en: Don't forget to put on sunscreen.
She puts on makeup every morning.

senses.meaningEn: to gain weight

examples.en: I put on three kilos over the holidays.
He's putting on weight since he stopped running.
examples.ko: 그는 달리기를 그만둔 뒤로 살이 찌고 있어.

senses.note: put on weight = gain weight. 반대는 lose weight.

senses.meaningEn: to remove clothes or shoes

examples.en: Please take off your shoes at the door.
It's hot. Take your jacket off.

senses.meaningEn: to leave the ground and start flying

examples.en: The plane takes off at nine thirty.
We're taking off soon, so turn off your phone.

senses.meaningEn: to not go to work for a period of time

examples.en: I'm taking Friday off to see the doctor.
Why don't you take a few days off?

senses.note: take + 날 + off: take Monday off, take a week off.

senses.meaningEn: to stop trying to do something

examples.en: Don't give up. You can do it!
examples.ko: 포기하지 마. 넌 할 수 있어!

examples.en: I almost wanted to give up on learning English.

senses.note: give up on + 사람/일 = ~을 포기하다, 단념하다.

senses.meaningEn: to stop doing or having something, especially a habit

examples.en: My dad is trying to give up smoking.
examples.ko: 우리 아버지는 담배를 끊으려고 노력 중이셔.

examples.en: I'm trying to give up sugar.

senses.note: give up + 동명사: give up smoking (O), give up to smoke (X).

senses.meaningEn: to take care of a person or animal

examples.en: Can you look after the baby for an hour?
examples.ko: 한 시간만 아기 좀 봐 줄 수 있어?

examples.en: Who looks after your dog when you travel?
examples.ko: 여행 갈 때 강아지는 누가 돌봐?

senses.note: 미국에서는 take care of 를 더 많이 쓰고, look after 는 영국에서 더 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: to be responsible for something

examples.en: Could you look after my bag for a minute?
examples.ko: 잠깐 내 가방 좀 봐 줄래?

examples.en: She looks after the shop when the owner is away.
examples.ko: 사장님이 없을 때는 그녀가 가게를 맡아.

senses.meaningEn: used to tell someone to hurry or to encourage them

examples.en: Come on, we're going to be late!
Come on, you can do it!

senses.meaningEn: used to show you do not believe or agree with someone

examples.en: Come on, that's not true.
Oh, come on. Don't be like that.

senses.note: 말투에 따라 '설마', '왜 이래', '제발' 등으로 뜻이 달라짐.

senses.meaningEn: to start working, especially a light or machine

examples.en: The lights come on at seven every evening.
The heater comes on when it gets cold.

senses.meaningEn: to stop working or studying for a short time to rest

examples.en: Let's take a break and get some coffee.
You've been studying for hours. Take a break.
examples.ko: 몇 시간 동안 공부했잖아. 좀 쉬어.

senses.note: take a rest 보다 take a break 가 훨씬 자연스러움. take a short break / take a coffee break.

senses.meaningEn: to do something wrong by accident

examples.en: Don't worry, everyone makes mistakes.
I always make mistakes when I rush.

senses.note: 동사는 do 가 아니라 make: do a mistake (X). 실수를 '하다'라고 해서 do 로 쓰는 흔한 오류.

senses.meaningEn: to enjoy yourself

examples.en: Did you have a good time at the party?
Have a good time on your trip!

senses.note: 작별 인사로 Have a good time! / Have fun! 을 자주 씀. have a great time 은 더 강한 표현.

senses.meaningKo: 아주 쉬운 일, 식은 죽 먹기
senses.meaningEn: something that is very easy to do

examples.en: The test was a piece of cake.
Don't worry, fixing this is a piece of cake.
examples.ko: 걱정 마, 이거 고치는 건 아주 쉬워.

senses.note: 항상 a piece of cake 로 씀. 실제 케이크 한 조각이라는 뜻과 구별은 문맥으로.

senses.meaningEn: to relax, calm down, or not work too hard

examples.en: Take it easy. Everything will be okay.
The doctor told me to take it easy this week.
examples.ko: 의사가 이번 주는 무리하지 말라고 했어.

senses.meaningEn: used as a casual way to say goodbye

examples.en: See you tomorrow. Take it easy!
Okay, take it easy, man.

senses.note: 미국 구어에서 친한 사이의 작별 인사. 격식 있는 자리에서는 피함.
